answer: Admission difficulty is priced by remaining seats, not by a fixed puzzle. (1) A joiner stakes a name commitment whose hash must fall under target T. (2) A keeper recomputes T hourly as 2^-k, with k = 8 + occupied/64, so each seat taken narrows the gate. (3) Effort per key doubles every 64 admissions: the first costs 256 hashes, a batch of 1000 fakes costs about 10^9. (4) Seats are leased for 30 epochs, so a parked hollow army must climb the ladder again. No prism splits T, it is global; a vine of resold keys only moves that debt. The door tightens as the room fills.
